title: B-tree lookup and split
brief: Show a complete lookup before opening a node; then insert a key that forces a split. Use one running example. Complete the whole flow before opening its pieces. Include spoken narration; label illustrative states as illustrations.
audience: Software engineer comfortable with basic programming and algebra, new to this mechanism. Define formal terms on first use.

sources.revision: Original curated classic B-tree example; not a B+ tree implementation

constraints.description: Ordering, search path, separator placement and fanout all checked on an executable fixture.

constraints.description: A concrete purpose/example and full end-to-end journey appear before internal machinery and equations. Each zoom refers to an established box and returns to the whole.
An animated split that loses a key, invents a disk-read count, or presents a stylized layout as a measured trace fails.

constraints.description: Essential words, diagrams, equations and causal motions are readable without clipping or distracting collisions at the target viewing size.

transferQuestions: Follow a new key not shown in the film and justify the path.
